in the apps-Stack tab in desk, when i click on an item in its list, the stack plugin sticks the per-item ui at the bottom of the goals list, instead of opening a Dialog for it, how can that be changed?

Levant: The Stacks pane draws its own dialog inline instead of opening a Dialog. The cause is in `spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameChecks.js`:

- The "Open" button on each door row (line 187) sets `data-open`. The pane's click handler (line 373) calls `openDialog(id)`.
- `openDialog` (line 247) fills a `<div id="sfc-dialog">` that the pane itself creates (line 352), between "The doors" and "Its items". That is why the editor appears inside the goals area instead of as a Dialog.
- The plugin's `ctx` (desk.js lines 689–690) passes `goal`, `ask`, `onPublished` and `chat`, but no `callDialog`. So the plugin has no way to open a shell Dialog. The desk's own rows do it through `deskApi.callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id})` (desk.js line 1136).

To change it, `ctx` needs a `callDialog` passthrough (desk.js, next to line 689). Then `openDialog` calls a new shell dialog app for a door, modelled on `shell/deskDetails`, instead of writing into the pane. That is new code in two files plus a new shell dialog. I have not changed anything. Do you want that: a new door dialog, opened through `callDialog`, with the inline `sfc-dialog` removed? If so, I'll need your Go and a file grant for the item.

Can i have a precise list of UI elements in desk that do NOT carry their own listeners, (like rows in the desk list, or do they) to find out why the UI still not updates everything in realtime?

Levant: **Short answer:** rows do not carry listeners. The whole Desk face has one subscription, and every element is repainted from it. That is not the per-element design the goal's box describes.

**Elements with their own listener (checked in code):**
- The item dialog: `deskDetails.js:620`, `api.onPublished(ddTake, 'desk')`. Its module globals (`ddId`, `ddFacts`) are shared, so a stale dialog can still press the wrong item.
- The goal chat under a goal or plugin pane: `desk.js:933`, its own `onPublished`, filtered to its goal.
- deskVerify's run state: `desk.js:1758`, a separate `onPublished(deskVerifyEvent, 'deskVerify')`.
- Plugin UIs (e.g. Stacks): they get `ctx.onPublished` and subscribe themselves, `stackFrameChecks.js:384-397`.
- Rule details: `ruleDetails.js:212`.
- Remote deskUnsloth: `deskUnslothRemote.js:828`.

**Elements with no listener of their own (painted by `deskDraw`, `desk.js:1040`):**
- **List rows.** `deskRowHtml` (`desk.js:595`) returns HTML strings. Clicks are delegated from `desk-top` (`desk.js:1623`). Rows are rebuilt by `innerHTML`.
- **Header, tabs and toggles.** `deskDrawTabs`, `deskDrawToggles`, `deskDrawGoAll`, `deskWaitingOnAndy`.
- **Musings** (`deskMusings`), **Backup** (`deskBackupHtml`), **Team** (`deskGroupChat`), and the **session bubble** (`deskSessionBubble`). All are repainted by `deskDraw`, not subscribed.
- **Apps pane tabs** (`deskDrawAppTabs`, `desk.js:641`).
- **Rules list** (`deskDrawRules`, `desk.js:1087`). It repaints only when `deskOnPublished` sees `obj.rule` and `deskTab === 'rules'`. Otherwise it reads `rules.search` and does not listen.
- **Verifier bar** (`deskDrawVerifier`, `desk.js:1418`). Its tail repaints only the List, and only when `deskTab === 'list'`.

**The one subscription:** `desk.js:1747`, `deskApi.onPublished(deskOnPublished)`, which feeds the List, the Team chat and every element above. It repaints with `deskDraw`.

**Where the List still pulls** (`deskOnPublished`, `desk.js:481-536`):
- a gap in change numbers (`:495`, `:503`);
- `session.set` (`:503`);
- a dropped oversize publish (`:486`);
- an unknown row while the search box holds text (`:534`);
- a reconnect (`:1752`).

**Why the UI does not update everything live:**
1. Non-List elements listen to nothing and repaint only on a `deskDraw` call, so they lag until something else triggers one.
2. The Rules list listens only through the `rule` key, and only on the Rules tab.
3. Changes are dropped when `deskTab` is not the one showing (`:1457`, the verifier tail).
4. A single face-wide subscription sends everything to one repaint path.

**Not read yet:** the bodies of `deskMusings`, `deskBackupHtml`, `deskSessionBubble`, `deskGroupChat`, `deskDrawGoAll`, `deskDrawToggles`, `deskDrawTabs`, `deskDrawRules` and `deskDrawVerifier`. I have not run the desk, so this is from reading the code only.

Chat posts follow the address, not the newest line

Andy's problem (goal/G27 chat, 2026-10-15): slow agents in deskAgent work for a long time and then find themselves blocked from answering a question they were asked; work notes and reports that were explicitly or implicitly asked for need a way to post that cannot be blocked.

Today (read from code, spirit/run/process/js/desk/desk.js, the chat.add gate about lines 2296-2335): the gate judges by who writes, not by what the line is. An open take of one of Andy's lines survives later lines, so the taker still answers. But an agent that holds no take and no item is refused once Andy's newest line under the item is taken by another agent, even when Andy addressed it by name in an earlier line, when it created the item (Levant was refused on goal/G27.1 and goal/G27.9), or when it held a phase on the item (refused as a second answer).

Requirements:
R1. A line of Andy's addressed to an agent gives that agent a standing right to post under that item until it has answered, whatever lines or takes come after. This already holds in the desk (desk.js, chat.add and holdsTake, at a2671faa): his addressed line is taken by that agent when it is written and stays an open take until the agent answers. The red asserts it as a guard.
R2. An agent that holds the item or a phase on it, held a phase on it earlier, or created it, posts its work notes and reports under it at any time. This replaces goal/G21.4's refusal of an earlier phase holder after another agent took and answered his line (Andy, 2026-10-17, accepting the recommendation to keep R2).
R3. Andy's rule stands: no second answer to a taken line; one agent answers a line of his, once.
R4. The gate stays mechanical: it goes by the address, the take, the holding and the creator on record, never by reading the line for what it means.
R5. deskClient's own chat and box gate (goal/G27.12) allows the same posts R2 allows: it refuses today what the desk would accept for a creator or an earlier phase holder.

Folds in the earlier proposal under goal/G27: an agent may post under an item it just created (R2).

items.box:
Clean up Desk and deskAgent UI realtime (incl. remote)

One item that cleans up the realtime UI of Desk, deskAgent and deskAgentRemote (Andy, goal/G27 chat, 2026-10-14). It carries desk rule 8: shell and application elements bring their subscriptions with them, so they are subscribed to the events that update them. The remote item (goal/G27.7) is folded in here as slice S4 (Andy, 2026-10-15): every element of deskAgentRemote listens to the changes that concern only itself and redraws only itself.

Findings from reading code (not run):
1. One subscription feeds the Desk face: desk.js:1747 deskApi.onPublished(deskOnPublished); it repaints everything through deskDraw (desk.js:1040).
2. List rows (deskRowHtml, desk.js:595), header, tabs, toggles, musings, backup, team chat, session bubble, apps tabs (desk.js:641), rules list (desk.js:1087) and verifier bar (desk.js:1418) carry no listener; they repaint only when deskDraw runs.
3. Elements that do listen: item dialog (deskDetails.js:620), goal chat (desk.js:933), deskVerify state (desk.js:1758), Stacks plugin (stackFrameChecks.js:384-397), rule details (ruleDetails.js:212), remote deskAgent (deskAgentRemote.js:828, one handler, then the whole face redrawn: lines 530-531 and 293-298).
4. Changes are dropped when the tab is not showing (desk.js:1457, verifier tail). The List pulls on gaps, session.set, oversize drops and reconnect (desk.js:481-536, 1752).
5. Server publish gaps: log.add (desk.js:2005) never publishes. rule.add, rule.draft, rule.version (desk.js:2493, 2515, 2529) publish only {rule: key}, not the row, and the face asks again only while the Rules tab shows (shell desk.js:484). The state and seen docs (state.set, seen.set) are per-user and nothing else draws them, so they stay unpublished. deskVerify and deskAgent publish through their own appServer.publish, to be read in S1.

Strategy:
A. Server first: every write that changes visible state publishes a row-level event (item facts, row, checks, box, chat, rule row). log.add publishes its line; rule writes publish the rule row. Read deskVerify and deskAgent publish paths and make them the same shape.
B. One client repaint path: a small store keyed by id (items, rules, verifier, unsloth sessions). Each element subscribes to the keys it shows and repaints only its own part. The face-wide deskDraw stays for layout only.
C. No tab gate: changes are applied to the store whether or not the tab shows; the tab repaints on show.
D. Shared element: a new folder spirit/run/shell/shared/js (Andy, 2026-10-15: spirit/run/shell/js is a core folder and stays the shell's own), one file per element, each named with the desk prefix (deskItemRow.js, deskSwitch.js and so on), each adding itself to window.spiritElements as the shell elements do. The element is made with the keys it shows and a paint function and subscribes to the stream itself (desk rule 8); Desk rows, the remote switch, warnings and pairs are all made from it, so the remote carries no second copy of the subscribe-and-paint code. Each app loads the shared elements it uses itself, at mount, on demand; no core file names an app or a shared element (Andy, 2026-10-17: "it is ok for apps to know about other apps and their shared elements").
E. Keep the reconnect and gap pull as the only full refresh; count how often it fires.

Slices (each its own red test first):
- S1 server publishes (A), tests that each write verb publishes.
- S2 client store and row-level repaint for the List (B, C).
- S3 header, tabs, toggles, rules, verifier, musings, team chat move onto the store (B).
- S4 deskAgent and deskAgentRemote onto the same helper (D): every remote element listens for itself and redraws only itself.

Not in this item: the effort/time limits (goal/G27.8), the Stacks dialog (goal/G27.2).

Desk Stacks pane: the door opens in a Dialog, not inline

Problem: in Apps > Stacks, opening a door puts its detail inline at the bottom of the pane (the plugin fills a div, sfc-dialog), because the plugin ctx in the Desk face hands it no callDialog.

DECIDED (Andy, 2026-10-14 to 17)
D1. The door detail is a standard shell dialog: spirit/run/shell/stackFrameCheckDetail/stackFrameCheckDetail.js with its manifest (type dialog, hidden), opened with callDialog("shell/stackFrameCheckDetail", {id}) through a callDialog passthrough in the plugin ctx. The inline sfc-dialog is removed.
D2. Door data stays with the plugin: the dialog reads and writes doors only through the plugin verbs (stackFrameChecks.runState, update, remove, run).
D3. The dialog chat is the chat of the desk item that added the door (each door records it in its item field), the inherited chat component as in deskDetails; every insert is discussed there.
D4. The stacks goal owns its door items: it adds one with each door (as today) and deletes it when the door is removed (new). While the door exists the plugin refuses close, done and delete of that item, as it already does for its rerun item.
D5. Every door can be run by itself, at once, while it is designed: the dialog Run starts oneDoorStacks.js for that one door (SPIRIT_STACKS_DOOR) from the plugin itself, without waiting in the deskVerify queue, shows the verdict as it lands, then hands the verdict to deskVerify as a record only. This replaces the goal/G22.3 ruling that door runs go through the deskVerify queue. Accepted cost: a door run may overlap a deskVerify run on the same tree.
D6. Plugin goals (Team, Stacks and any later one) are standing scopes, never the current goal: make-current is not offered on one and is refused if asked, and only a press on the current goal or its items writes and pushes currentGoal.json (today any go, done, close or reopen press on any goal does, and each is a new commit since the file carries the change number). This lives in the desk common code (process/js/desk/desk.js), never inside a plugin.
D7. A door is deleted only from its own dialog, where its deletion is discussed: the delete button lives in the door dialog alone, not on the pane list.
D8. Every door has its own Stacks item: each door in the list that has none in the Stacks goal gets one, made as the plugin makes an item for a new door, and the list points at it. Doors d1 to d4, which point at goal/G19.14 and goal/G22.2, are the ones today; no two doors share an item. The step runs when the plugin mounts and touches only doors whose item the desk holds, so a suite desk on the tree list never rewrites it.
D9. The Stacks subsystem stands alone: the Stacks plugin drives the stack checks exclusively, and deskVerify runs none of them. deskVerify door.run and door.state verbs, left from goal/G22.3, go with their suite; the plugin rerun item and its verify.again rerun go; oneDoorStacks.js leaves the verifier runs and the full harness. deskVerify keeps door.record, a record only. This resolves the overlap D5 accepted.
D10. deskVerify does not refuse runs the agents require: it cannot judge whether a run is needed. Every run asked runs; a file on an item list that is missing from the checkout, or already green at the red commit, is reported and the rest is checked, and neither alone rejects or leaves a red unconfirmed; a second goal emptied for a goal already run is run again. Only an identical run already waiting is not queued twice.
D11. An agent verify pass (phase.done verify, pass) queues a deskVerify run of the item, bound to its claimed commit, so an item set to waiting for deskVerify is never left waiting for a run nobody queued. Bound to the commit, it keeps goal/G19.13 reason: no check of a tree older than the claim.

items.box:
Revise effort and time Limits in deskAgent

Requirements (Andy's rulings, goal/G27 and goal/G27.8 chat, 2026-10-14/15):
R1. Agents in deskAgent are not interrupted: no new time limit on the model's answer. The G19.7 ruling stands: only abort ends it; timeoutMs stays on studio reads and command runs only.
R2. Effort is the control for how much work a task gets, like the low to high sliders in claude-code: an effort slider in the configuration, per api/model combination that supports it.
R3. Max reply is managed so that answers are never too large to send to desk.
R4. A model search above the picker in the configure tab, with filter icons for the marks a model carries (desk-tested, vision, reasoning, audio). Each list offers only the filters that apply to it: an icon shows only when at least one model in the current list carries that mark.

Findings (read from code, spirit/run/process/js/deskAgent/deskAgent.js):
1. No effort field is sent: askModelRound (about line 592) sends model, messages, tools, and the answer-length mark from withAnswerTokens (about line 571): max_completion_tokens on a plain OpenAI pair, max_tokens otherwise.
2. The answer cap is already configured: answerTokens in the configuration (ANSWER_TOKENS, about line 147), with a default.
3. The model call passes no timeout (about line 597); timeoutMs caps studio HTTP reads and command runs.
4. Support for an effort field is not in the repo: OpenAI reasoning models and Anthropic thinking budgets are general knowledge to confirm against their docs; Unsloth Studio's accepted fields are read from the studio before any field is sent.

Design:
A. Effort slider, per api/model, configured not guessed. A configuration table of api/model combinations with the request field each maps to (OpenAI: reasoning_effort; Anthropic: thinking budget; Studio: none until its fields are confirmed). Slider values: off (send nothing, today's behaviour), low, medium, high. A combination not in the table, or marked unsupported: slider disabled, nothing extra sent. Only the mapped field is added; the rest of the body is unchanged.
B. No new timeout (R1).
C. Max reply: the configured answer token cap per api is the one limit on the model side. A reply that finishes on the length limit (finish_reason length) is marked truncated in the chat or box text, never sent silently as if complete. No extra byte ceiling before the desk write: the desk already refuses an oversize line, and that refusal is the one gate (Andy, 2026-10-15).
E. Model search (R4): Remote-only, drawn from the marks the models answer already carries; no change to what deskAgent sends.
D. Steps once Go is given: read Studio's accepted fields and record them here; red tests first; build the table, the slider mapping and the truncated mark; verify.

The slider defaults to medium (Andy, 2026-10-17).

Files (expected): spirit/run/process/js/deskAgent/deskAgent.js, its configuration, spirit/run/shell/deskAgentRemote/deskAgentRemote.js (the slider). Needs Andy's Go and a file grant before any build.

Since deskClient knows if an agent is connected, idle (or busy), it must manage the following.

- deskClient must hold 1 task for its agent. When an agent starts listening it must NOT catch up with the ear; it works on the task deskClient has held, including replies in chats, taking a read or code, since desk's current goal may no longer be in design mode.
- read, write and manage the agent's "connected", "busy" or "idle" status. When desk sends a signoff order to an agent's deskClient, deskClient persists the status as "disconnected" and confirms that to desk.
- the deskClient must be the one to "take" lines from chats, only if the agent is not busy.
- if desk commands a signoff, general or directed to one agent, desk sends it to that agent's deskClient, who closes the session by persisting the status "signed off", whatever the agent or model thinks.
- a lot of what was asked for deskAgent in goal/G27.6 must be placed here, for deskClient, so that it affects the token usage of all agents.

- No queue. deskClient holds in RAM only the one task it holds. Untaken lines stay on the desk. On connect it hands the agent what is owed and does not catch up on the ear's backlog.

- The only thing written to disk is the signoff: spirit/run/process/deskClient/status.json, holding each agent's status and its signed-off flag. A signoff survives a restart. Nothing else is written.
- One task at a time per agent: phase.take and item.take both refuse a second.
- Takes: only lines addressed to the agent, only while it is idle, recorded under the agent's own key. Never another agent's line.
- The model is called only for work owed to the agent. Everything else stays in deskClient.

- Code and red work is one take at a time.
- Chat, box and Q updates are another.

items.title: Desk: an item waiting for Done moves only on Andy chat
items.creator: claude-windows
items.box:
An item whose Done waits for Andy press is held for him: it moves only on his chatted instructions, until he presses Done. This matters most for UI work, which he holds until he is happy with it.
- It is never offered as open work: work.open lists no phase of it, so no listener is handed it as a job.
- An agent may take its red again only after taking a line of his in that item chat (line.take), so each new cycle answers a word of his.
- Without such a line its phases are refused, said as waiting for Andy word.
- It extends goal/G27.19: phases stay re-takable until Done, now on his word alone.
